subject: subsetting inside dplyr and applying a different function

messages.author: 44307ae45eab113b
messages.subject: subsetting inside dplyr and applying a different function
parts:
Hi glad if someone can help me with this.

I want to apply a different chi-square test to subset of my data frame, inside the dplyr ecosystem.
So far the only way to have what I want is to do it separately and bind rows after.
But I am sure there is a nice way to do this.

First subset, PATTERN with "abxac":

pattern.A <- genotypes.summary %>%
  filter(PATTERN=="abxac") %>%
  group_by(LOCUS) %>%
  do(
    CHISQ=chisq.test(c(.$aa,.$ab, .$ac, .$bc), p = c(0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25), simulate.p.value=T, B=1000)
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    GOF = CHISQ$statistic,
    GOF_PVALUE = CHISQ$p.value
    ) %>%
  select(-CHISQ)

Second subset, PATTERN with "abxab":

pattern.B <- genotypes.summary %>%
  filter(PATTERN=="abxab") %>%
  group_by(LOCUS) %>%
  do(
    CHISQ=chisq.test(c(.$aa,.$ab, .$bb), p = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.25))
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    GOF = CHISQ$statistic,
    GOF_PVALUE = CHISQ$p.value
    ) %>%
  select(-CHISQ)

Third subset, PATTERN with "aaxab" and "abxaa":

pattern.D <- genotypes.summary %>%
  filter(PATTERN=="aaxab" | PATTERN=="abxaa") %>%
  group_by(LOCUS) %>%
  do(
    CHISQ=chisq.test(c(.$aa,.$ab), p = c(0.5,0.5))
    ) %>%
  mutate(
    GOF = CHISQ$statistic,
    GOF_PVALUE = CHISQ$p.value
    ) %>%
  select(-CHISQ)


The only thing different between the 3 subset of "genotypes.summary" is the CHISQ test (goodness of fit) applied to the subset "abxac" and "abxab" (in bold).

pattern.A, pattern.B and pattern.D  return data frames with 3 columns that could be bind by rows (the chi-square is applied by rows (by LOCUS))

Question: I sure there is a nicer and shorter way to apply the different CHISQ to the data set at once?

Thanks
Thierry
